name: Napoli 2015-18 (Sarri)
scopeNote: SSC Napoli under Maurizio Sarri (appointed 2015-06-12, left 2018-05-23, neither a match date). Period runs from the first competitive match, Sassuolo 2-1 Napoli on 2015-08-23 (Serie A opener, confirmed by Corriere dello Sport and Forza Italian Football), to the last match of 2017/18, Napoli 2-1 Crotone on 2018-05-20 (from a search summary of FourFourTwo/Sky/SI, not mined, so unverified). Style named 'Sarriball' / Juego de Posicion (Spielverlagerung). Evolution: 2015/16 started 4-3-1-2 (Valdifiori, Insigne behind two strikers) and moved to 4-3-3 from the Europa League match of 2015-09-17, Higuain 36 goals; 2016/17 Mertens centre-forward from October 2016 after Higuain's sale and Milik's injury; 2017/18 same 4-3-3 with Mertens, 91 points. Popular label 'zonal marking' is partly an inference: sources describe ball-oriented positional defending (tier C), no source mined states Sarri's marking in those words, and a FanSided piece calls the shape '3-5-2', which looks wrong. 2014/15 (Benitez) and 2018/19 (Ancelotti) facts excluded; SBS/beIN items post-date the period but describe Sarri-era habits and are flagged retrospectiveOnly where relevant. Partial dates (month or season) used where the exact day was not found.
openQuestions: Marking: no tier A-B source mined explicitly says zonal for Napoli's back four; evidence is ball-oriented 'positional defending' (translated analysis) and high line. Confirm with a dedicated zonal source.
FanSided calls the formation a 3-5-2; other sources say 4-3-3 with a temporary back three in build-up. Treated as a labelling error.
Last match date 2018-05-20 (Napoli 2-1 Crotone) rests on search summaries only; kick-off times differ between sources.
Exact dates for the Chievo corner (3-1) and the Inter 3-0 (Dec 2016) matches not confirmed; month or season used.
Who pressed/covered in 2017/18 specifically: little tier A-B coverage of 2017/18 itself; much 2017/18 detail comes from 2016/17 or retrospective pieces.
Contested rotation narrative: De Laurentiis blamed Sarri's lack of rotation (beIN, 2018-07); Sarri defended it (Goal, 2017-10).

sources.evidence: From goal-kicks Napoli occupy positions in order to give Reina as many passing options as possible with their staggered positioning that creates width and depth.

sources.title: Team Analysis: Napoli (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Firstly they rotate into something resembling a 3-4-3, with Jorginho dropping onto the same line as Koulibaly and Albiol (often remaining slightly higher) while Ghoulam and Hysaj push on and join Hamsik and Allan in the second line.

sources.title: Team Analysis: Napoli (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Higuain, Insigne and Callejon maintain fairly high positions to stretch the opponents' vertically while the touchline hugging full backs stretch them horizontally.

sources.title: Team Analysis: Napoli (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: In all phases of their possession game Napoli show a clear focus on disorganising their opponents with their strategic use of possession in true Juego De Posicion style.

sources.title: Team Analysis: Napoli (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: In mid and deep block defensive phases the ball near 8 is usually responsible for pushing up to engage the opposing ball carrier. When pressing against the opponents' build-up however the ball-near players often sit back and cover while the responsibility to create access falls to the ball-far 8 and ball far winger. In these moments Napoli often move into highly compact, lop sided 4-3-3/4-3-1-2 situational structures.

sources.title: Team Analysis: Napoli (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Due to the far side being practically vacated if Napoli's press is beaten they will struggle to shift to the opposite flank in time to prevent the opponents from taking advantage of the space.

sources.title: Team Analysis: Napoli (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Man-marking however seeks to pitch the game into a series of 1v1 duels and at times Napoli have not been able to adapt their methods to be effective against this. This was evident in the recent loss to Udinese

sources.title: Team Analysis: Napoli (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: When Insigne receives the ball he has various actions to choose from including shooting, crossing or dribbling, this unpredictability makes him difficult to defend against.

sources.title: Napoli - Inter Milan 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)

sources.title: Napoli - Inter Milan 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)

sources.title: Napoli - Inter Milan 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Where beforehand he would stay in the 2nd line of Napoli players, Jorginho moved between the centre-backs during build-up with an increasing frequency.

sources.title: Napoli - Inter Milan 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Their counter pressing was strengthened with greater numerical superiority in midfield which allowed them to both attack and defend with more control.

sources.title: Sarri's Napoli in rampant home victory (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: One of the biggest offensive characteristics of Sarri's Napoli is using central progressions to create space in wider areas. This takes advantage of the inevitable pressure that follows a vertical progression.

sources.title: Sarri's Napoli in rampant home victory (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: This movement is in line with a general rule Sarri has instilled, namely; players who are covered move forwards whilst a nearby team-mate drops.

sources.title: Sarri's Napoli in rampant home victory (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: A common rotation in Napoli's game model sees Hamsik move deep in the left half space, Ghoulam move to an advanced wing position and Insigne high in the left half space.

sources.title: Sarri's Napoli in rampant home victory (Spielverlagerung)

sources.title: Sarri's Napoli in rampant home victory (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Pioli's side attempted to press Napoli with a distinctly man-oriented approach, particularly in midfield.

sources.title: Clash of contrasting strategies in Napoli's draw with Juventus (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Napoli resumed their typical high press. The strategy was effective in reducing the threat that their visitors carried, as Juventus created just four shots - which was partially a result of many of their possessions not crossing the halfway line. Napoli's forwards would continue to close down Juventus' build-up all the way back to Buffon

sources.title: Clash of contrasting strategies in Napoli's draw with Juventus (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Although it didn't completely shut-down Napoli's left-sided attack, Juventus provided good resistance to their opponents' game and reduced the amount they were able to play the ball inside the block.

sources.title: Clash of contrasting strategies in Napoli's draw with Juventus (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: As a result of Juventus' tight defence, Napoli's approach to the penalty area became slightly more direct than usual. Sarri's team were able to maintain possession well around Juventus' block, but struggled to create gaps

sources.title: Clash of contrasting strategies in Napoli's draw with Juventus (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: This tactic was used successfully three or four times to enable Napoli to find Insigne and Mertens between the lines.

sources.title: Maurizio Sarri: Coach Watch (Coaches' Voice, 2024 retrospective)
sources.evidence: During 2015/16 as their senior striker, Higuaín scored 36 goals in 35 appearances in Serie A, and often because of their impressive ability to build possession in wide territory. He remained advanced for as long as possible

sources.title: Maurizio Sarri: Coach Watch (Coaches' Voice, 2024 retrospective)
sources.evidence: They were particularly fluid towards the left (above), where they regularly progressed possession via quick combinations and rotations and runs from a third player. Faouzi Ghoulam advanced from left-back, and the right-footed Dries Mertens or Lorenzo Insigne, as their left-sided forward, drifted infield

sources.title: Maurizio Sarri: Coach Watch (Coaches' Voice, 2024 retrospective)
sources.evidence: Towards the right they were considerably more direct; José Callejón, as their right-sided forward, attacked around the outside of opponents to provide crosses or, if play was unfolding towards the left, moved infield to operate alongside Higuaín as a second striker. Elseid Hysaj largely resisted attacking from right-back, and instead featured in what temporarily became their back three.

sources.title: Maurizio Sarri: Coach Watch (Coaches' Voice, 2024 retrospective)
sources.evidence: Jorginho was Napoli's defensive midfielder, and was supported by Allan, who also moved deeper to contribute to recovering the ball. They regularly complemented Hamsik's forwards runs by forming a double pivot. Jorginho also orchestrated a significant amount of their deeper build-up

sources.title: Maurizio Sarri: Coach Watch (Coaches' Voice, 2024 retrospective)
sources.evidence: When Higuaín later left for Juve, Mertens, partly owing to injuries suffered by Arkadiusz Milik, featured as their central attacker, and Insigne consistently started towards the left.

sources.title: Maurizio Sarri: Coach Watch (Coaches' Voice, 2024 retrospective)
sources.evidence: His players' familiarity with his methods meant Sarri's team accumulating a club record 91 points in Serie A - the most of any runner up in the competition's history.

sources.title: Maurizio Sarri: Coach Watch (Coaches' Voice, 2024 retrospective)
sources.evidence: Sarri's Napoli applied a particularly aggressive press that often resembled the shape of Chelsea's. The younger Higuaín, and later Mertens, worked across the pitch to press the in-possession central defender, and attempted the direct their pressure wide to prevent switches of play and to force possession to one side of the pitch

sources.title: Maurizio Sarri: Coach Watch (Coaches' Voice, 2024 retrospective)
sources.evidence: Napoli's central midfielders most commonly prioritised their closest opponent, which meant Allan often advancing ahead of Jorginho to alongside Hamsik.

sources.title: Maurizio Sarri: Coach Watch (Coaches' Voice, 2024 retrospective)
sources.evidence: Napoli, like Chelsea, regularly recorded a strong grasp of possession, and therefore made numerous regains via their counter-press and the ability of those offering cover to make regains after attacking players had conceded the ball in the final third; Allan's tenacity, and Jorginho's ability to read their opponents, were crucial to their success.
